article_content: ISNA - Iranian Students' News Agency Tue / 14 November 2023 / 11:59 Iran's Foreign Minister Hossein Amirabdollahian held a heartfelt discussion with his Hungarian counterpart, Peter Szijjarto, focusing on enhancing bilateral ties and addressing the dire situation in Palestine amid Israel's relentless bombardment of Gaza. Tehran (ISNA) - In a compassionate appeal, Iran's Foreign Minister Hossein Amirabdollahian called for urgent international intervention during a phone call with Hungary's Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto. The conversation centered on strengthening relations between the two nations and the escalating Middle East crisis, particularly the devastating impact of Israel's attacks on Palestinian civilians. Amirabdollahian vehemently condemned Israel's actions as 'egregious violations of humanity,' stressing the catastrophic consequences of their military aggression in Gaza. He urged the global community to pressure Israel to cease its offensive immediately, enforce a ceasefire, and ensure unhindered access for humanitarian aid to Gaza. Citing alarming data from the Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor, Israel has dropped over 30,000 tonnes of explosives on Gaza since October 7, equivalent to three nuclear bombs. The Gaza Health Ministry reported that over 15,000 Palestinian lives have been lost due to Israel's indiscriminate attacks. Amirabdollahian also highlighted the promising trajectory of Iran-Hungary relations, expressing eagerness to host a joint commission in Tehran to solidify cooperation. Szijjarto reaffirmed Hungary's commitment to nurturing this partnership and exploring mutual growth opportunities. article_content: Carsten Spohr, Chairman of the Executive Board and CEO of Deutsche Lufthansa AG, says: 'We would like to thank our customers and the employees of the Lufthansa Group for a challenging summer: With the lowest revenue and profit ever achieved in one summer - including an operating loss of 1.5 billion euros in the third quarter alone. All airlines in our Group and Lufthansa Technik contributed to this with single-digit profit margins. At the same time, employee satisfaction in our company has declined significantly to the lowest level since the crisis. It is costing us all that we have combined our unsuccessful multi-airline and multi-hub strategy with weakening the private travel segment, setting the wrong strategic course. We have also made significant setbacks in operational stability and regularity despite favorable conditions. This trend is the basis for missing our premium and quality standards and those of our customers even more effectively in the future again. Even though the geopolitical situation remains stable, our booking outlook gives us reason to be concerned - not only for a very poor Group result this year, but also beyond.'
